title: Local copy: the Board survives a reload
lede: The Notes are saved to localStorage and come back on reload. On startup `main.tsx` reads the **Local copy synchronously and loads it before the first render**, so a reload never flashes an empty Board. After that, `saveLocalCopy` **subscribes to the Notes store** and writes the whole Board 300 ms after the last change, with a **flush on `pagehide`** so closing the tab straight after typing loses nothing. What is read back goes through `parseNotes`, a hand-written guard: a damaged copy is discarded with a warning, never half-loaded.

files.question: When is the Local copy read, and when does saving start?
files.summary: The composition root loads the Local copy into the store before `render`, then starts saving with the real `window` timers and wires `flush` to `pagehide`.
files.owns: The order: read, load, subscribe, render. The real `localStorage` and timers.
files.never: Decides what is valid or when to write: that is `src/persistence/`.
files.tested: By hand in a real browser (reload, close-then-reopen, a damaged copy). `renderApp` in the browser tests leaves the Local copy out.

files.question: What is stored, and when is it written?
files.summary: `readLocalCopy` reads and checks the `{ v: 1, notes }` envelope; `saveLocalCopy` debounces writes off the store's subscription and returns `flush`.
files.owns: The storage key, the format, the 300 ms debounce, and swallowing storage errors.
files.never: Touches `window`: storage and timers are passed in.
files.tested: Node tests in `localCopy.test.ts` with a fake storage and fake timers the test moves on itself.

files.question: Which Notes from outside the app are trusted?
files.summary: `parseNotes` turns `unknown` into `Note[]` or `null`: all or nothing, unknown fields dropped.
files.owns: The shape of a valid Note: a non-empty id, finite numbers, a string text, a known colour.
files.never: Clamps or rounds: `load` commits each rect inside the Board, as for any other Note.
files.tested: Node tests in `parseNotes.test.ts`, one per way to reject; each guard was mutated to check a test fails.

files.question: Why does a no-op never save?
files.summary: Unchanged. `load` was already there. Every action `set`s a pure transition, and one that changes nothing returns the same state, so Zustand notifies no subscriber.
files.tested: Its own tests; `localCopy.test.ts` checks a no-op writes nothing.

scenarios.name: A reload brings the Board back

steps.title: The page loads, before anything is rendered
steps.explain: The read happens at module top level, before `createRoot(...).render`. `getItem` is synchronous, so the first render already has the Notes. Saving is started only after `load`, so loading the copy never schedules a write of what was just read.

steps.title: Each saved Note is checked
steps.explain: Every field is checked, and the result is built from the checked values only, so an extra field in storage never reaches the store. One bad Note returns `null` for the whole list.

run.from: const { id, text, colour, z, ...rest } = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
run.to: return { id: noteId, ...rect, text, colour, z };

steps.title: The Notes go into the store, then the first render
steps.explain: `load` keeps the order in which the Notes were saved, which is `ids` order (creation order, also DOM order), and recomputes `topZ` from the saved `z`s, so the Stacking order comes back exactly. Then the first render paints them.

scenarios.name: Typing, then closing the tab at once

steps.title: Each keystroke changes the store
steps.explain: Each `setText` returns a new state, so Zustand calls the subscriber, which restarts the 300 ms timer. A burst of keystrokes therefore makes one write, 300 ms after the last.

steps.title: pagehide, less than 300 ms later
steps.explain: The timer would never fire in a closing page, so `pagehide` calls `flush`, which writes now and cancels the timer. `pagehide` rather than `beforeunload`: it also fires for the back/forward cache and never blocks leaving. Checked in Chromium through Playwright: two Notes typed and the page closed with no wait, and nothing was in storage before the close; on reopening both were back.

run.from: const copy: LocalCopyV1 = { v: 1, notes: ids.flatMap((id) => notes[id] ?? []) };

steps.title: pagehide with nothing scheduled
steps.explain: When the Board has been still for 300 ms the timer has already written and cleared `scheduled`, so `flush` returns at once: no second, identical write. The test 'writes a scheduled save at once when flushed, and only once' covers both halves.

scenarios.name: A damaged copy, or a full storage

steps.title: Startup with a copy that can't be trusted
steps.explain: Not JSON, `getItem` throwing, a version other than 1, no `notes`, or one invalid Note: each is a warning and an empty Board, never a crash. The copy isn't deleted; the next save overwrites it. `localCopy.test.ts` has one case per cause.

run.to: console.warn('Discarding the Local copy: it could not be read.', error);
console.warn('Discarding the Local copy: it is not a valid version 1 copy.', raw);

steps.title: A write that throws
steps.explain: A full quota or blocked storage throws from `setItem`. It is swallowed, so the timer callback can't throw an uncaught error, and the next change tries again. The test 'keeps saving after a write fails' makes one write fail and the next succeed.

run.to: // Quota exceeded or storage blocked: nothing to do but keep working in memory.

steps.title: The browser blocks site data altogether
steps.explain: Reading `window.localStorage` itself throws when site data is blocked. Then there is no Local copy at all: one warning, and the app works in memory as before.

run.to: console.warn('localStorage is blocked: Notes will not survive a reload.', error);

notes.title: The key is `sticky-notes:local-copy`, not the issue's `sticky-notes:cache`
notes.detail: The glossary lists "cache" as a word to avoid for the Local copy, and the key shows in DevTools. Renamed before anything was released, so no copy under the old key needs migrating.

notes.title: A trailing debounce, not a throttle
notes.detail: Continuous typing for longer than 300 ms between pauses never writes until a pause. That is acceptable because `pagehide` flushes; the counter-argument is a browser crash mid-burst, which loses the burst.

notes.title: Not Zustand's `persist` middleware
notes.detail: It would remove `saveLocalCopy`, but the format, the `parseNotes` guard and the flush on `pagehide` are the parts worth controlling. Recorded in ADR 0002.

notes.title: No browser test for a reload
notes.detail: The round trip (save, read, load, identical state) is a Node test, and the reload was checked by hand in Chromium. `renderApp` deliberately has no persistence, so the browser tests start empty.

notes.title: No REST saving, and no traces of it
notes.detail: The MSW worker, its handler and the one `GET /notes` that `main.tsx` sent at startup and only logged are deleted, with the `msw` dependency and `apiBaseUrl`. The Local copy has no `unsaved` field: REST saving (bonus V) is out of scope, so nothing in the code or docs is built for it. The app is now one chunk with no top-level `await`.
